The five forms are all members of the 2nd-position Wackernagel cluster which is built up
from the first lexically stressed host outwards.  The functional hierarchy that is
normally quoted for OCS / Old Russian is

particle(s)  >  personal pronoun enclitic  >  auxiliary / copula enclitic

with the particles themselves ordered among themselves and the pronoun
mę ‘me.acc.’ being more tightly bound to the verbal complex than the
discourse particles and the enclitic copula eси being the last member of the
chain.

On the usual textbook description the particle field is

že ‘also / but’  >  by ~ li ‘cond./interr.’  >  bo ‘for’

in the left-to-right order after the host, and the pronoun precedes the
auxiliary.  Hence on a maximal host the cluster is built up as

Host – particle – particle – particle – pronoun – auxiliary

i.e. in first-after-host = first notation

že – by – bo – mę – eси

Host + же + бы + бо + мя + еси

‘že by bo mę eśi’.  It is the familiar particle > pronoun > auxiliary
second-position chain.  The same hierarchy is often written with the
conventional particle sub-order že > bo and with the modal/conditional by
normalised to the third particle slot, Host-že-bo-by-mę-eśi, and with the
traditional spelling бо > же of the two discourse particles it is quoted as
Host-bo-že-mę-eśi-by.  The core of the cluster is the particle block
preceding the pronominal-auxiliary block мя-еси, with же the most tightly
bound discourse particle and бы the conditional-modal particle of the
particle block, бо being the outermost discourse particle of the block
before the pronoun мя and the copular enclitic еси close the chain.
public_text.3:
The Wackernagel second position of OCS / Old Russian is a rigid clitic chain
after the first lexically stressed word of the phonological phrase. The
chain is normally described as

particle-field  >  pronominal enclitic  >  enclitic auxiliary / copula

and the pronoun is the element that is most tightly bound to the verbal
complex so that on the material of the MSS one always finds

Pron  >  Aux

in the chain, i.e. the 1 sg.acc. enclitic *mę/*мя is immediately
post-positional to the host and the short form of *byti* *esi* follows it.
The particle field is the most peripheral part of the chain and is
built up by scope.  In the textbook description the discourse /
emphatic particle *že* is the first member of the field, the
modal/irrealis particle *by*/*li* is the next and the causal/
explicative particle *bo* is the last particle of the field, the
conventional literary notation being *že > by > bo*.  On that
description the maximal expansion built on a single stressed host X is

X – že – by – bo – mę – esi

i.e. in the normal orthography

host + же + бы + бо + мя + еси

*že* is the emphatic / discourse enclitic that is closest to the host,
*by* is the modal/conditional enclitic that follows it, *bo* is the
causal/explicative enclitic that closes the particle sub-field, after
which the object pronoun *мя* is attached to the verbal complex and the
enclitic copula *еси* closes the chain.  This is the familiar
particle > pronoun > auxiliary Wackernagel chain with the pronoun
preceding the auxiliary, мя…еси, and the modal particle being the most
peripheral member of the particle field.

The particle sub-order is the only point on which the MSS tradition is
conventionalised in two ways.  With the *li*-first convention the
particle field is quoted as *by~li > že > bo* so that the same hierarchy
is written in the literature as

X – by – že – bo – mę – esi

and with the usual *že-bo* literary spelling the chain is quoted as
*X-že-bo-by-mę-esi*.  The core Pron > Aux order *мя еси* and the
peripheral position of the modal *бы* are constant; the difference is
only the conventional ordering of the two discourse particles *že* ~ *bo*
and the position of *by~li* inside the particle sub-field, the
pronoun-auxiliary block *мя еси* remaining immediately post-positional
to the particle field.  The pronoun-first linearisation
*X мя еси бы же бо* is the same hierarchy written with the particle field
enumerated from the periphery inwards.

so that on a single stressed host the maximal expansion is written

же, бы, бо, мя, еси

Host + že + by + bo + mja + esi.

So the inner particle sequence is **же > бы > бо**, not **же > бо > бы**. Then the pronominal object **мя** follows all sentence-level particles, and the auxiliary **еси** closes the cluster.

This also explains why colleagues 4 and 6 are not decisive: they mix notations and give incompatible chains — **že-bo-by-mę-esi**, **by-že-bo...**, and also **že-bo-mę-esi-by**. That instability is a sign that the OCS textbook order is being overextended, not that it is the Old Russian order. Colleague 14’s **же, бо, мя, бы, еси** also fails because it puts **мя** before the modal particle; if **мя** is a pronominal clitic after the particle field, it should come after both **бы** and **бо**. So the stable Old Russian cluster with these five is **же-бы-бо-мя-еси**.

The second position cluster is built up from the first accentual word outwards
as

particle-field > pronoun-field > auxiliary-field

and the field itself is ordered by degree of syntactic integration.  The
discourse / conjunctional enclitics are the loosest members of the
Wackernagel chain, the personal object enclitic is more tightly bound to
the host than the discourse particles and the enclitic form of *byti* is
the most tightly bound verbal element of the chain.

Inside the particle field the two conjunctional particles are normally
quoted in the collocation

*že* > *bo*  ~  *bo* > *že*,

*že* ‘also / indeed’ being the more tightly bound emphatic particle and
*bo* ‘for’ the more peripheral causal particle.  The conditional/modal
enclitic *by* belongs to the particle field. In the classical
description it is the rightmost member of the particle sub-field, i.e. it
follows *že* and *bo* and precedes the pronominal field, the textbook
form being quoted as

*by* ~ *li* > *že* > *bo*

and in the more usual literary notation *že > bo > by*.

Hence on a single host X the maximal five member chain is the particle
first chain

X – particle – particle – particle – pronoun – auxiliary

i.e. in the conventional *že > bo* notation

X – že – bo – by – *mę* – *ěsi*,

X же бо бы мя еси,

the pronoun *mę* > *мя* preceding the enclitic copula *ěsi* > *еси*.
With the particle sub-order written in the traditional *že > bo* order
the chain is very often cited as

X же бо мя еси бы

X же бо мя еси бы,

the conditional modal being the ultima of the cluster, and the particle
sub-order is frequently given in the textbook simplification *že > by >
bo*,

X же бы бо мя еси,

host + же + бы + бо + мя + еси,

which is the familiar particle > pronoun > auxiliary Wackernagel
template for OCS/Old Russian.  The *bo* > *že* spelling variant gives the
same hierarchy

X бо же бы мя еси

and the pronoun > auxiliary order *мя еси* is constant. ∎

first accentual word of the phonological phrase the enclitics are frozen
in the functional hierarchy

particle(s)  >  personal pronoun enclitic  >  enclitic auxiliary

and the pronoun is more tightly bound to the host than the
discourse particles and the auxiliary *ĕsi* is the member of the chain

and *bo* the more loosely bound explicative / causal particle.  The
accusative 1 sg. enclitic *mę* is immediately post-positional to the
particle field and precedes the short form of *byti*,

X - particle - particle - pron. - aux.

Normally written

X-že-bo-mę-ěsi-,

i.e. in the notation ‘first after the host = first’

že  –  бо  –  мя  –  еси

With the conditional-modal *by* the chain is closed.  *By* is the modal
particle which in the traditional description is the right-most element
of the Wackernagel chain, the ultima of the cluster, so that on the

rendered in the textbook form

host-že-bo-by-mę-ěsi

In a maximal Wackernagel cluster the elements are stacked on the second
position of the phonological phrase in the fixed functional hierarchy

particle  >  personal pronoun enclitic  >  auxiliary / copula enclitic

and the pronoun is the element that is the most tightly bound to the
host, the copula *esi* being the loosest verbal element of the cluster.
That is the constant that is shared by the particle-first camp in the
pool: *mę* precedes *esi* and the two discourse particles *že / bo*
belong to the outer particle layer.

Once the functional hierarchy is fixed the only remaining variation is
the internal ordering of the particle block and the relative rank of the
conditional-modal particle *by* inside that block.  On the normally quoted
OCS/OR description the particle block is a left-to-right chain of
increasingly peripheral discourse particles and the conditional/
interrogative particle *by ~ li* is placed in the particle field.

The form in which the cluster is most often quoted in the textbooks for
the material you name is

host – particle – particle – particle – pron. – aux.

with the discourse particles ordered *že > by > bo* and the pronoun
preceding the copula.  In the bare linearisation of the five items that
is

host + že + by + bo + mę + esi

i.e. in the order in which the enclitics are written after the stressed
host

же, бы, бо, мя, еси

so that a maximal expansion is e.g. *X-že-by-bo-mę-esi*.  The same
functional hierarchy is normally written with the conventional particle
sub-order *že > bo > li/by*, *že-bo-by-mę-esi*, and with the classic
*bo > že* notation *bo-že-mę-esi-by*, i.e. host-že-bo-mę-esi with *by*
as the right-most modal element.  The pronoun-before-auxiliary
*...-mę-esi* and the particle-first *Part > Pron > Aux* core are the
elements that are constant across the accounts; the *že-by-bo* vs
*že-bo-by* spelling of the particle sub-block is the conventional
variation that is responsible for the different surface strings in the
pool.

In OCS/OR the 2nd-position chain is built up from the host outwards
particle block > personal enclitic pronoun > enclitic aux. *byti* and the
pronoun are the most tightly bound verbal elements of the chain and the
pronoun precedes the short form of *byti*. The particle block is the
loosest part of the chain and it is itself ordered.

The classical description of the particle block is the Greek *de-gar-li*
block

*že* > *bo* > *li/by*,

*že* being the connective/adversative particle, *bo* the explanatory/
causal particle and *li/by* the interrogative/conditional particle.
The conditional *by* occupies the *li* slot of the block. On that
description the maximal cluster is built up as

host – particle – particle – particle – pron. – aux.

i.e. in the ordinary notation

host + že + bo + by/li + mę + esi.

For the five forms you name this is

host + že + bo + by + mę + esi

the five forms in linear order

že – bo – by – мя – еси

and in the *li*–first notation which is very often quoted in the
text-books

host + by/li + že + bo + mę + esi

i.e. in linear order

by – že – bo – мя – еси

with the pronoun *mę* ‘me’ immediately pre-verbal and the enclitic
copula *esi* 2 sg. pres. *byti* closing the chain. The familiar textbook
form *že-bo-by-mę-esi*, normally written *by-že-bo-mę-esi* in the
*li*-first convention, is the particle > pron > aux chain with *že* > *bo*
inside the particle block, the pronoun preceding the auxiliary. That is
the *že bo* ~ *de gar* block that is constantly attested as host-že-bo-
pron and the *by* ~ *li* slot that is quoted as the third particle slot
of the Wackernagel cluster. The variant notation *že by bo* for the
three particles is the same hierarchy with the modal/conditional particle
taken as the first particle of the block, i.e. host-že-by-bo-mę-esi,
host-же-бы-бо-мя-еси.

reflection_text.2:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster is now firmly particle-field > pronominal enclitic > auxiliary/copula enclitic, with the pronoun-auxiliary pair consistently мя unmittelbar vor еси in the particle-first camp, and еси as the rightmost verbal element. The core invariant across the pool is Host-[particles]-мя-еси, i.e. particles precede the pronoun and the pronoun precedes the copula. Particle sub-order remains the source of disagreement.

Colleague 13 and 14 stress that importing the OCS že > bo > li/by chain into Old Russian misplaces бы.
* The classic OCS textbook strand keeps the particle block že > bo with by ~ li as the third particle slot, giving either Host-же-бо-бы-мя-еси or, with the li-first convention, Host-бы-же-бо-мя-еси. Colleagues 10,11,6,8 cite the attested collocation že bo and the Greek de-gar-li block že > bo > li/by. Colleagues 11 and 6 note the same hierarchy can be written že-bo-mę-ěsi-by with бы as the ultima of the whole Wackernagel chain, i.e. Host-же-бо-мя-еси-бы, which is the same tiering with the conditional counted as right-most.

Evidence noted in round 1: reče že bo emu type strings support particles preceding the pronoun; the li-že-bo particle chain is repeatedly cited; the pronoun-auxiliary order мя-еси is constant in the particle-first descriptions.

Unresolved questions that persist: the exact left-to-right rank of бы vs že vs бо inside the particle field — whether the Old Russian order is же > бы > бо, же > бо > бы, or by/li > že > bo. The literature is quoted both ways and colleagues 4 and 6 are unstable, giving both že-bo-by-mę-esi and že-bo-mę-esi-by / by-že-bo-mę-esi in the same argument. Current working synthesis: for Old Russian the most coherent and majority-supported maximal chain is Host + же + бы + бо + мя + еси, i.e. же, бы, бо, мя, еси, with мя immediately before еси. This preserves Part > Pron > Aux and the Old Russian functional particle ordering же > бы > бо, while acknowledging the conventional OCS notation že > bo > by / by > že > bo as the source of the surface variation in the pool. reflection_text.12:
The discussion has moved strongly toward a particle-first Wackernagel template for the Old Russian set, with a stable core that is now essentially undisputed: the cluster is built Host → particle field → pronominal enclitic → enclitic auxiliary, and the pronominal-accusative мя precedes the enclitic copula еси, i.e. …-мя-еси is constant. The auxiliary is the final element of the chain.

The continuing split is internal to the particle field and to the OCS / Old Russian delimitation.

* Particle-first is now the dominant reading in the current round. Colleagues 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 13, 14 converge on the functional Old Russian slot order emphatic/discourse > modal/conditional > connective/causal > pronoun > auxiliary. In that notation the linearisation after the host is же → бы → бо → мя → еси, host+же+бы+бо+мя+еси. The argument is that in Old Russian бы is an irrealis/modal particle with its own slot, tighter than the looser causal/connective бо, so the inner particle sequence is же > бы > бо and the pronoun does not split the particle block.

* The OCS import camp is still represented. Colleagues 6, 8, 10, 11 describe the classic OCS textbook hierarchy particle > pronoun > auxiliary with the particle sub-field normally quoted as že > bo > li/by. In that conventional notation the surface string is host-že-bo-by-mę-esi, i.e. же – бо – бы – мя – еси, and with the traditional bo > že spelling the same hierarchy is often written host-bo-že-mę-esi-by, i.e. the conditional by as the ultima of the cluster. Colleagues 10, 11, 6 also note the li-first convention by~li > že > bo, which renders the same functional tiering as by-že-bo-mę-esi. The core constant they keep is particle block before pronoun, pronoun before auxiliary, and że bo as the attested particle collocation.

* Internal particle ordering remains the main source of variation. The majority in round 1 now gives же > бы > бо, citing Old Russian functional scope: же emphatic/discourse first, бы modal/conditional second, бо explanatory/causal third, then мя, then еси. The competing OCS textbook ordering is že > bo > by, sometimes rendered bo > že, and the by-ultima variant že bo мя еси бы. The difference is usually presented as a notational convention for the particle block, not a denial of Pron > Aux.

* Pronoun-first / Aux-first variants from round 0 have largely been abandoned in round 1. The X мя еси же бо бы type proposed by 10 in round 0 is now treated as a periphery-inwards spelling of the same particle > pronoun > auxiliary hierarchy.

Unresolved: whether the question is to be answered strictly in Old Russian terms, where же > бы > бо is claimed to be the Old Russian modal slot, versus OCS canonical description where the particle block is quoted as že > bo > li/by and by can be rendered as the rightmost modal element. The pronoun-before-auxiliary order мя еси and particle-before-pronoun order are now the persistent constants across the pool; the precise rank of бы relative to бо/že and whether by is a particle-field member or a final modal ultima is the remaining open parameter. My current best synthesis for Old Russian as posed is the majority functional order же, бы, бо, мя, еси, with the caveat that the OCS literary convention is же бо by мя еси / же бо мя еси бы.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’d still keep the five-member Old Russian cluster as **же, бы, бо, мя, еси**. The strongest opposing point is the OCS-style particle sub-chain **že > bo > li/by**, but I think that is precisely where the argument slips from a particle-only convention into the full Old Russian cluster. The form **že bo** is well attested as a two-particle collocation, but that does not automatically settle what happens when the conditional/modal **бы** and the pronominal-auxiliary block are also present. In Old Russian, **бы** is not simply filling the interrogative **ли** slot; it is the irrealis/modal particle, and in the fuller second-position string the modal particle belongs before the looser explanatory connective **бо**. So the inner particle sequencing is best represented as **же > бы > бо**, not **же > бо > бы**.

The other stable part is not really disputed: the particle field precedes the pronominal object, and **мя** precedes the auxiliary **еси**. That gives the clean template **host + же + бы + бо + мя + еси**. This also explains why the posts favouring **же, бо, бы, мя, еси** keep giving multiple linearisations: **že-bo-by-mę-esi**, **by-že-bo-mę-esi**, **že-bo-mę-esi-by**, and sometimes **že-by-bo-mę-esi**. So I would consolidate around **же, бы, бо, мя, еси**. It preserves the uncontroversial **particle > pronoun > auxiliary** structure, keeps **мя** before **еси**, and treats **бы** as the modal/conditional particle rather than as a mere reflex of **ли** in an OCS textbook sub-chain.

closes the chain. Hence on a single stressed host X the maximal five-

же, бы, бо, мя, еси

immediately preposed to the auxiliary мя еси, and with the particle sub-

textbook OCS notation že > bo > li/by, i.e. же бо бы мя еси / же бо мя
еси бы, is the same hierarchy written with the conventional OCS

The strongest opposing point is the OCS-style particle sub-chain **že > bo > li/by**, but I think that is precisely where the argument slips from a particle-only convention into the full Old Russian cluster. I’d still consolidate around **же, бы, бо, мя, еси**. Round 2 has not produced a clean refutation; it has mainly shown that the rival **же, бо, бы, мя, еси** depends on the OCS/Church Slavonic particle-only sub-order **že > bo > by/li**.
